title: A Comprehensive 3D-Molded Bone Flap Protocol for Patient-Specific Cranioplasty
protocol: Patients should lie in a supine position with their head first into the gantry.
Maintain teeth occlusion during the imaging acquisition process.
Avoid swallowing or chewing during the scan.
Center the table height such that the external auditory meatus (EAM) is at the center of the gantry.
Adjust the patient’s head position within the field of view (FOV) to ensure the region of interest (ROI) lies within the FOV boundaries.
Use a vertical occlusal plane by positioning the lowest available head rest.
Acquire images using a larger FOV for higher quality imaging of specific ROIs.
Position the scan angle parallel to a line created by the supraorbital ridge and the inner table of the posterior margin of the foramen magnum when possible.
Utilize radiopaque markers to determine the orientation of CT scan images.
Adjust gantry tilt for sequence scanning as available, but note that it is not available for spiral or dual source scanners.
Download CT scan data from scanner workstations.
Save files in DICOM format for subsequent editing.
Transfer DICOM files to an Additive Manufacturing Unit.
Ensure sufficient RAM and read performance for processing large DICOM files.
Segment the bone from other tissues in the CT scan images.
Convert segmented 2D images into a 3D mesh to generate volumetric reconstruction.
Establish a relationship between the ‘glued’ contact surfaces of the skull and the prosthesis using Hypermesh® software, with the skull as the “master” and the prosthesis as the “slave”.
Evaluate prostheses resistance under three different static loading conditions: 50 N, 600 N, and 1200 N.

Apply a 50 N load perpendicularly to a circular region defined in the center of the PMMA prostheses, based on an approximation of the reaction force induced in the skull when resting on a flat surface (≈ 5 kg).
Simulate extreme impact conditions by applying a 1200 N load perpendicularly to the same circular region.
Apply a 600 N load as an intermediate value between 50 and 1200 N, perpendicularly to the specified circular region of the PMMA prostheses.
Fix the contour of half of the skullcap to prevent translation and rotation on an xyz-coordinate axis.
